dct_description_sm: This multi-year project aimed at gathering and disseminating information of climate change risks to community infrastructure in the Northwest Territories (especially in the case of permafrost degradation). The specific objectives of the project were: (1) to compile current information related to permafrost degradation and infrastructure in the Northwest Territories; (2) to classify the information collected and create a database available to communities to provide a better understanding of what has been done and where; (3) to develop a Best Practices summary of assessments, and adaptation approaches for community governments; (4) to identify gaps in the information needed for communities to be able to assess the vulnerability of their infrastructures; (5) to prepare a long-term work plan for addressing gaps; (6) to identify potential funding sources for communities to address site specific vulnerability assessment of their infrastructure; and (7) to communicate this information effectively to communities and stakeholders.   In its second year (the second phase), focus was directed on identifying, collecting, and classifying (in a database) information relating to permafrost degradation in the Northwest Territories and its effect on infrastructure. This database was made available to all communities (via internet), giving them the capacity to assess and evaluate the vulnerability of their infrastructure. In addition, a Best Management Fact Sheet was created to inform and educate communities on the subject.
dct_subject_sm: Social sciences, economics and policy -> Adaptation
dct_title_s: Vulnerability Assessment of Permafrost Degradation on Community Infrastructure in the NWT
